title: He Cut Down the Oldest Tree on Earth

voice.engine: kokoro-82m (onnx) — SCRATCH timing reference only, never published

lexicon.bristlecone: B R IH S AH L K OW N

scenes.name: Alive through one strip of bark
Revelation: older than the Great Pyramid

lines.text: In {1964|nineteen sixty-four}, a student cut down the oldest known tree on Earth.
lines.delivery: Quiet and grave, like the first line of a true-crime story. Slow down on 'the oldest known tree on Earth'.
Matter-of-fact, defending him a little. Small beat after.

lines.text: He was a scientist, and he needed to count its rings.
lines.delivery: Even and reasonable: it sounds like a perfectly good idea.

lines.text: So, with permission, they cut it down.
lines.delivery: Flat, almost reluctant. Then silence: the tree falls in that pause.

lines.text: Then he counted: {4,844|four thousand eight hundred forty-four} rings.
lines.delivery: Slow and precise on the number, a touch of awe. Let it hang.

lines.text: Bristlecone pines survive by letting most of the tree die.
lines.delivery: Curious, slightly darker tone on 'letting most of the tree die'.

lines.text: This one was alive through a single strip of bark.
lines.delivery: Soft, almost tender. Lean on 'single strip'.

lines.text: Their rings are so reliable, scientists used them to correct carbon dating.
lines.delivery: Impressed, a little proud of the tree. Crisp on 'carbon dating'.

lines.text: Another one, Methuselah, is still alive in California.
lines.delivery: Turn the page: lighter, a hint of hope on 'still alive'.

lines.text: It was a seedling before the Great Pyramid was built.
lines.delivery: The revelation. Slow right down on 'before the Great Pyramid was built' and let it sink in.

lines.text: Its exact location is a secret.
The Forest Service won't say which tree it is.
lines.delivery: Plain statement. Tiny pause before the next line.

lines.text: The last time we found the oldest tree on Earth...
lines.delivery: Trail off with the pitch suspended: the video loops straight into 'In 1964, a student cut down the oldest known tree on Earth.'
